newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ONFEM says no shr placement needed in 97.
newsitem.headline: ONFEM says no shr placement needed in 97.

text.p: ONFEM Holdings Ltd said on Friday it has sufficient cash on hand for its acquisition plans after disposing of all its holdings in Oriental Metals (Holdings) Co Ltd and should not need any share placements in 1997.
"We have realised more than HK$470 million from the disposal of all our interest in OrientMet," Jia Yuan, deputy mananging director, told reporters in a news conference.

This will enable the firm to further invest in industrial projects involving high technology that show good earning potentials, he said, adding the group should not need to seek additional funding through stock placements in 1997.
The company also expected to get more than HK$100 million from the exercise of warrants by their holders when they expire in August, executive director Guy Look said.

"Together with the proceeds from the sale of Oriental Metal shares, we will have more than HK$600 million on hand," Look said. "So at this stage, we can't see any reason why we should raise more money," he added.
Yuan said the company was in talks to invest in a number of projects, mainly in China.

"In new high technology and new materials investments, we are studying a number of projects, including in areas of rare earth metal...hard alloys and rare and precious metals," Yuan said. Details would be announced later, he added.
ONFEM sold a 40 percent interest in Oriental Metal to its parent China Nonferrous Metals Holdings (Hong Kong) Ltd for HK$354.5 million in January.
ONFEM subsequently disposed of all its remaining 10.8 percent stake in Oriental Metal, the nonferrous metal trading firm, in the open market, an executive director Guy Look said.
"Our parent company, China National Nonferrous Metals Industry Corp (CNNC), now has two major listed companies, one is ONFEM and the other one is Oriental Metal," Yuan said.
He said the two companies would have a clear division of work with ONFEM focusing in high new technology and new materials as well as specialist construction, property and trading businesses.
Oriental Metal would be at the same time developing its base metals trading and related investments.
